name: Allied Digital Services Ltd
title: Allied Digital Services Ltd - 532875 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Revenue up 20% to Rs 968 cr but PAT growth rests on a Rs 21 cr deferred tax credit after a one-time ECL provision; no supply-side discipline, and management guides 20-25% growth with margins 12.5-13% targeted.

summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 20% to Rs. 968 crore, with adjusted EBITDA of Rs. 112 crore (11% margin) after a one-time ECL provision.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q4 and FY26 revenue of Rs. 968 crore (up 20% YoY), with India up 17% (Q4 India up 37%) and international up 22%. Reported PAT rose 10% to Rs. 36 crore, helped by a Rs. 21 crore deferred tax asset benefit, while PBT was hit by a one-time ECL provision of around Rs. 36 crore. Management said the auditor qualifications from the FY25 Q4 report have been withdrawn, with the Section 186 loan matter pending RBI approval. Government revenue fell 6% in FY26 and management blamed tender delays and equipment cost spikes linked to the Iran-Israel conflict.

financial_highlights.change: +20% YoY vs Rs. 807 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA FY26 (ex one-time ECL provision)

financial_highlights.value: 30% = Rs. 1.50 per share on Rs. 5 face value

financial_highlights.metric: New orders and renewals in Q4

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY in FY26. Management wants Services at 75-80% of revenue because contracts run about 5 years and provide annuity visibility.

segments.name: Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 17% YoY in FY26. Management describes it as the entry point for larger annuity-led Managed Services; its share rises during implementation phases.

segments.name: Enterprise customers
segments.commentary: Revenue up 31% YoY in FY26, now the main growth driver.

segments.name: Government customers
segments.commentary: Revenue down 6% YoY in FY26; management expects a meaningful rebound in FY27-28 after Q4 tender delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% to 25% YoY (management says internal target is more aggressive); long-term aim of 10x in 10 years.
Short-term EBITDA margin target of 12.5% to 13% (Nehal said 12% first, then higher); long-term target 13% to 15%.
Tax rate for FY27 expected around 25%, plus or minus 1-3 points depending on deferred tax benefit.
Auditor qualification expected to be cleared within about two quarters, once RBI approval on the Section 186 loan-to-equity conversion comes through.
Mumbai government contract (Rs. 150-200 crore, 9-month implementation plus 5-year O&M) to be announced in about 2-3 weeks; management says it is still being finalised.
capex_capacity: Multiple projects were in the capex phase in Q4, raising equipment supply and direct expenses by about 3-4% versus the standard level.
Western Railway project (orders of Rs. 165 crore and Rs. 85 crore) was dropped after equipment costs rose 25-30%; retender expected by mid-July, with bidding to follow.
Maharashtra pipeline of about Rs. 2,000 crore-plus; two large government contracts worth Rs. 600 crore each expected as RFPs within two quarters, with the company a front runner.
Noida Smart City and various high court and digital projects are also in the pipeline.
demand_pricing: Q4 new orders and renewals were about Rs. 166 crore, with wins in smart city command-and-control, deep-sea oil drilling managed services and multi-region workplace services.
Management said industry-wide margin pressure exists and is being offset by AI and AIOps deployments that cut delivery costs.
Government tenders were delayed by the Iran-Israel war and equipment costs spiked; management says pricing has since stabilised.
Management says no client has yet moved work in-house due to AI; outsourcing demand is rising. It expects 20-25% headcount reduction per customer over 6-12 months from AI deployment.
Competitors reportedly bidding at lower prices; management said client interactions are going well.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients deferring spend, and how will the revenue-versus-margin mix look given peer price competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Nehal said client interactions are decent. Margin pressure is industry-wide; the company is offsetting it with AI and AIOps, which he says lowers delivery cost and improves margins after onboarding.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India growing while government projects decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Nehal blamed the Iran-Israel war for equipment cost spikes that forced the company out of some government bids. He said tender pricing has since stabilised and government traction is improving.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to clear the audit qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: Nehal said the loan-to-equity conversion is done and RBI approval is pending. He expects a clean report within about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did direct expenses rise to Rs. 585 crore from Rs. 467 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gopal said direct expenses are normally around 60% of revenue, and Q4 was elevated by roughly 3-4% from multiple projects in capex phase. Management also cited the one-time ECL provision of about Rs. 36 crore in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook and how much deferred tax benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Gopal said FY26 benefited from Rs. 21 crore of deferred tax asset credit. Some benefit will continue but not at the same level; Nehal guided the tax rate at about 25%, plus or minus 1-3 points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin path for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nehal said margins are about 11% now and the aim is 12-12.5% soon, then 13%, with 15% long term. Paresh said AI could cut resource count by 20-25% per customer over 6-12 months.

risks_watch: One-time ECL provision of about Rs. 36 crore and deferred tax credit make reported profit quality hard to read; FY27 PAT depends on whether these recur.
Government revenue fell 6% in FY26 and the Q4 government order flow was weak; the Rs. 166 crore order intake is a low base to judge FY27 growth.
Auditor qualifications depend on RBI approval for the Section 186 loan conversion; timing is uncertain.
Equipment cost volatility from the Iran-Israel conflict led to lost bids; management still needs to convert pipeline (Mumbai contract, Maharashtra RFPs, Western Railway retender in July).
Industry-wide pricing pressure and AI-driven productivity gains could compress margins before the 12-13% target is reached.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and governance, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the weak government segment, the one-time charges and margins. Several answers relied on future announcements (Mumbai contract, RBI approval) without firm dates.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong close to FY '26, delivering the highest quarterly revenue in Allied Digital's history in the fourth quarter.
So, from a guidance perspective, I would try to give anywhere between 20% to 25% growth.
We want to target it to anywhere between 13% to 15% on the long term.
So, we see definitely a reduction on the resource count for any customer close to 20%, 25% in a matter of 6 months or a year.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%), backed partly by Rs 166 crore Q4 orders and a pending Rs 150-200 crore Mumbai contract plus Rs 600 crore Maharashtra RFPs, but no physical capacity additions were disclosed and the Western Railway project was dropped.
